admirals.bio:
Prime Starchief Quetzalcoatl has been a bane of UCM and PHR forces for the entirety of the Reconquest. Far too often the forces of one of the branches of Humanity will be winning an engagement against the Scourge only for Quetzalcoatl to arrive with his fleet and engage the existing combatants. In short order Quetzalcoatl annihilates the Capital Ships in the area and will then quickly leave the engagement, handing the Scourge a crucial victory.

However, the very next day, as the Scourge seem close to victory, he'll reappear and destroy any Scourge Capital ships before they're able to retaliate and again leaves the area, handing victory to whoever is facing them. Quetzalcoatl's interference as part of a tribe that has not formally made itself known to the UCM shows that there are yet more Shaltari tribes that seek to prolong the conflict between Humanity and the Scourge.

No attempts at communication have succeeded, and he has been given a threat level of the highest priority, however currently, no one from the UCM or PHR have managed even the most cursory of communications with them, only gleaning the name from Pungari mercenaries that have themselves, only heard of Quetzalcoatl in name and reputation.

admirals.bio:
Mergen the Learned claims to have been alive long enough to have borne witness to the Shaltari's exodus from Aaru. Whether or not this is true can be left up for debate, but what is known is that this alabaster elder is an incredible tactician. Proving pivotal in the recapture of Aaru, Mergen was able to recall the exact sites of dormant Shaltari teleportation nodes. With this ancient knowledge Mergen's flagship, The Heart of the Mountain, was able to deploy vanguard battalions to critical locations ahead of the main Shaltari host.

In the void battles above the planet, Mergens fleet was responsible for sending a fifth of what Scourge remained above Aaru to their demise. The only other Starchief to achieve a similar number of confirmed kills was Quetzalcoatl, unsurprising given their martial prowess.

With the void above Aaru all but captured, Mergen is able to turn his attention to restoring the buried teleportation network on Aaru. Once his work on Aaru is done, the reclamation of other Shaltari strongholds awaits his attention.

admirals.bio:
Starchief Seth is part of a Shaltari Tribe that specializes in the use of Gravity weapons. The use of these esoteric Shaltari weapons is incredibly hard to plan against, it's easier to defend against a weapon that destroys you, but one that has you turning the wrong way and flying towards your own fleet is much more difficult.

Seth exemplifies these battle tactics of his tribe, his gravity weapons are more powerful than usual, a potentially unique modification in the otherwise standardized Shaltari arsenal. His ship will go in and out of orbital levels without any effort, allowing him to stage ambushes where, with a few well-placed shots, leaves an enemy battle plan in tatters.

His Sapphire Battlecruiser is a dreaded sight for any Reconquest leader, as soon as he is spotted, they know their best laid plans are already laid to waste. As often with the Shaltari, communication is erratic, and Seth has been known to engage in quite active communication at times, seemingly acting friendly, right up till he can activate his gravity weapons.

The twins have been sighted working alongside various tribes. Which has led UCM intelligence to believe they are some type of mercenary within Shaltari culture. However, their modus operandi is the same every time. Arriving in a pair of Amber class cruisers they will work with other cruisers and, via methods unknown to the UCM at this time, will increase the maneuverability of those ships giving the Shaltari fleet an unexpected advantage.

They are never seen separated, and even if one is destroyed, the next time they engage in fleet combat they'll be back together as a pair of Ambers. Causing chaos and disrupting even the most carefully laid plans by the Reconquest forces.

Any Communication with the Twins has seen them actively mocking and teasing any forces they are battling, seemingly enjoying the chaos they cause and the destruction with a relish that seems unnerving.

ship.lore:
Although many Shaltari ships can be considered unusual, the Bronze class battleship is especially so. At the prow, it mounts the fearsome Ion Cannonade - two vast rows of ion weapons with an excessive rate of fire. Like all ion weapons, these can cause havoc to a ship's power systems before battering it to shreds with a hail of energy pulses. On the ship's back, it mounts a Gravitic Beamer. While damaging enough on a basic level, this weapon's real threat comes from its effectiveness against ships in atmosphere and its tendency to literally shove ships forward, often into unfortunate places. Lastly, the ship mounts twin broadside crescents of microwave emitters for close-in killing power.

Unlike other, more focused battleships, this class requires a Starchief with flexible cunning to achieve its maximum lethality while frustrating enemy operations.

ship.lore: Closely related to the Bronze, the Silver class battleship also features a broadside microwave array and a prow-mounted Gravitic Beamer, but replaces the Ion Cannonade with the spectacular Obliterator Cannon. This massive weapon's capacitance prongs take up nearly half the ship's length. These generate a cracking flow of unstable, rare particles then channel them through a small emitter nozzle at the unfortunate target. For a Shaltari weapon, It is uncharacteristically random in its destructive power due to exactly how this torrent of particles interacts with its target. In the worst cases, they burrow through a ship like lightning through jelly, annihilating ordinary matter in their quest not to exist. Such a strike can cripple even another battleship, so only the most foolhardy captain would bank on a hit dissipating harmlessly around their ship's hull. Although most Starchiefs may be considered shrewd operators, those that command the Silver class may have an insatiable, gambler's mindset.

Unlike the familiar Platinum class, the Gold is a far more aggressive vessel, since it mounts the powerful, close-action microwave arrays of its sister classes. Also armed with the Ion Cannonade, the Gold is a terror to almost any vessel, and that's before its swarms of formidable Shaltari bombers strike. Certainly, the Gold is one the Shaltari's premier assets and a worthy chariot for the mightiest of attack-oriented Starchiefs.

ship.lore:
The Platinum Class shares the same basic hull design as the Diamond class, but its internal space and vast upper levels are dominated by an enormous flight deck, making this vessel a supercarrier by UCM reckoning. The Platinum class can unleash swarms of fighters and bombers in an unstoppable tide of destruction, in volumes and quality that few other ships can match. In addition (and like its cousin the Diamond) it also serves the secondary function of mothership, carrying a small number of ground troops to supplement surface landings.

Ships of this class are among the most ancient vessels ever encountered by mankind. Indeed, the very first non-human ship to make contact with humanity on the now famous exploration frigate Endurance was the Platinum class Supercarrier Aten. During the then cordial relations between Shaltari and Human, the Starchief at the helm of the mighty ship proudly proclaimed that it was over 7000 Earth years of age, and that was well over 300 years ago. Their continued survival over the millennia is due in part to their scale, but mostly to the extended combat range granted by its strike craft, ensuring that finally ending one of these behemoths is a challenging task in the extreme.

ship.lore:
The Diamond Class battleship is a truly frightening spectacle. Stretching 1546 meters in length, this mighty vessel is one of the largest known battleships and an imposing figurehead for any fleet. Despite their rarity, more UCMF officers ranking Admiral or above have met their deaths at the hands of one of these leviathans than any other type of ship in the Reconquest. This has caused many to speculate that the aliens use them to specifically hunt flagships, or simply that their captains treat the slaying of an opposite number as the highest achievement, such as it can be when fighting humans.

In addition to a pair of disintegrator banks, the Diamond class' primary armament is a triad of super particle lances. These vast weapons extend through half the ship's entire length and are fixed in the forward arc, such is their unknowable mass. These monstrosities have the ability to scythe through any armour like butter, their beams frequently passing right through a capital ship. While their damage dealing ability is potent, their real strength lies in reliability, the certainty that the enemy will feel the Diamond's wrath, no matter how well protected it is.

Coupled with the twinned Thermal Lance Cannons, this ship is at its most deadly when its captain, who must possess time-honed skill, can manoeuvre into an optimal firing position prior to unleashing all weapons, pushing the ship’s enhanced power matrix to the limit. This killing power is supplemented by a standard feature, thus far, of all Shaltari pocket battleships – launch clamps for self-deploying surface assets. These forward-facing weapons are devastating enough, but once the Euclase is in an optimal firing position, the full might of the ship’s cores can be focused though them, increasing firepower at the expense of manoeuvres. Given the drain on the power matrix, the Euclase’s other offensive capabilities are low drain launch options. A substantial fight deck accommodates swarms of fighters and bombers, while the vessel’s enhanced superstructure permits the carrying of self-deploying surface assets. Its ability to launch self-deploying surface assets forms the foundation for this, but the addition of twinned Ion Storm batteries enhances this mission profile. With these, the Painite can bombard surface positions to support its landings or direct the weapons’ coruscating energies against enemy vessels above the dropsite. Packing the full firepower of a battlecruiser in addition to its surface deployment mount, the Painite also mounts a linked pair of disintegrator batteries for devastating firepower during flexible manoeuvres. ship.lore: The Goethite is a more conventional, multi-role battlecruiser compared to its cousin the Hematite. It has also emerged recently, suggesting this may be a newly developed series. Its primary armament is a twin Hyperwave Cannon - a gigantic offshoot of the microwave-based weapons dreaded by infantry. In fleet terms, its closest equivalent is the far smaller arrays carried by Amethyst frigates, but this matches the range of conventional guns. The effect of hyper-concentrated microwaves on the target is stunning - a superheated mass of core superstructure results, which over time simply melts through the guts of the target, often destroying it long after the Goethite has moved on to a fresh target. The Goethite also carries a compliment of Shaltari fighters and bombers, providing flexibility in combat. Its captains often close to medium range, engaging large targets with the Hyperwave Cannons while dispatching smaller victims with waves of bombers.

It presents the firepower of four Chromium class destroyers in a frontal cluster of Thermal Lance Cannons - directed energy, long-burn weapons equivalent to the lasers of more primitive races. Hematites are preferred by Elder captains who relish the precision killing of a single, worthy foe. Being a battlecruiser, the Hematite is large but offers no other serious weaponry. In a one-on-one naval duel, there are few more terrifying opponents. Hastily issued UCMF combat doctrines dictate engagement preferably with squadrons of fast frigates, although ships that small are atomised in seconds if caught under the solar intensity of the quad Thermal Lance.

ship.lore: The Palladium and Sapphire class battlecruisers are more specialised than their conventionally aggressive kin and were conceived for disruption and close-range engagements. Although both classes aren’t commonly encountered, the Palladium is rarer than the Sapphire. Why this should be is uncertain, although the generally accepted theory is that the Adamant/ Palladium type hull is an ancient design no longer manufactured, having been superseded by the more recent Ruby/ Sapphire These vessels rely on a pair of ion storm generator banks to inflict crippling damage – equally devastating in the close action or orbital bombardment roles. Their second main armament is a pair of gravity coils. These forward-facing constructs create a localised, deadly beam of gravitic disturbance, ripping chunks from hulls, crushing bulkheads under their own weight, and even changing the heading of a multi-thousand-ton warship, disrupting the battle plans of any foe.

They lack a battleship's ability to take punishment, however, trading durability for speed, and so demand captains who employ dexterity, restraint and opportunistic aggression.

Much like its cousin, the Mesolite, this warship packs a battlecruiser-grade linked pair of disintegrator batteries for devastating firepower during flexible manoeuvres. While it offers little else in weaponry, it makes up for this with a docking mount for two stacked self-deploying surface instillations. These have already proven deeply problematic to deal with and represent an increased willingness from the aliens to commit to medium, and even long-term, surface commitments in contested territory. ship.lore: While Shaltari battlecruisers are regrettably familiar, some of their latest, lightest derivatives are not. Classified as supercruisers, these ships appear to be brand new. The alien’s choice to increase battlecruiser production and variety suggests a development, but whether that’s the strain or war or simply innovation is unknown. The first Shaltari supercruiser sighting, early in 2679, was the Mesolite. This svelte ship-killer is armed with a twin Hyperwave Cannon, matching the primary armament of the heavier Goethite class. It foregoes other capabilities though in favour of a mount for two stacked self-deploying surface instillations. These vary from the Stellargate, which brings starship-grade teleport technology to the surface, to the Electrowave Caster, a devilish weapons instillation capable of inflicting crippling damage on orbiting starships. The most awe-inspiring and outlandish is the Worldstrider – by far the largest known walker-type construct, thus far. This city block-spanning monstrosity smashes whole instillations beneath its six, tungsten-sheaved legs.

ship.lore: The Onyx is the most commonly encountered heavy cruiser of the Shaltari Tribes. Armed with a trio of disintegrator banks, the Onyx is capable of unleashing deadly amounts of firepower in the heart of any engagement, though it must surround itself with enemies in order to do so thanks to the limited firing arcs on its weapons. To make such a risky manoeuvre more palatable for the death-fearing Shaltari, the Onyx has a bulkier hull than standard cruisers, excellent point defence, and the ever-present Shaltari shield capabilities. Due to the awesome destructive power it possesses, command of an Onyx is frequently a stepping stone to greatness for starchiefs, winning their captains great renown and helping their legacy grow.

ship.lore: The Obsidian class heavy cruiser is one of the most feared ships in the Shaltari tribal fleets as it generally hunts the largest and grandest of prey. Crews of Obsidians take great honour in slaying opponents larger than themselves and many of the class’ captains have been subsequently elevated to Starchief. Enemy flagships, carriers and battleships are frequently targets for the Obsidian’s wrath, such is the concentrated nature of its awesome firepower. It is armed with a trio of forward facing particle lances – weapons of focused fury able to slice through any known armour with preposterous ease. Since armour serves virtually no protection against these weapons, they are frequently turned on the toughest, best protected ships in an enemy fleet, where this advantage is most telling. The only downside to these weapons is their lack of ultimate damage potential, although they more than make up for this in their ability to cause harm in a highly predicable and reliable way, making the Obsidian an excellent choice when the odds of failure must be minimised.

ship.lore: The Jet class heavy cruiser is one of the most flexible available to the tribal fleets. It can be applied effectively to a variety of missions and situations with its varied fire options making it equally effective at orbital bombardment, close action attack or ranged ship-ship action. The skill in utilising this class, as demonstrated by its best and most ancient of captains, is to put it in a position where more than one of these offensive means can be brought to bear simultaneously. Unusually, this seems to be a new class, with the first sighting only a few years before the Reconquest began, indicating that Shaltari technology is still evolving, albeit at a slower pace than other races. It is armed primarily with two banks of ion storm generators. These eldritch weapons generate waves of coruscating energy at close ranges and can be turned on ships (bypassing all point defences in the process) or on surface targets, lashing whole districts to rubble in seconds. For longer range ship- ship combat, the Jet is equipped with a single bank of disintegrators, which are normally used when closing in on the enemy with the combined fury with its other weapons.

Unlike troopships, motherships also carry a dropship equivalent (know as Gates) – small craft that are the final step in the chain before troops enter the battlefield itself. These materialise from the voidgates, fly to the dropzone and then ground units materialise from them. This complex system ensures that troops are never at risk in transit, preserving precious lives from defence battery fire.

ship.lore: The Basalt class fleet carrier is the Shaltari tribes primary launch vessel for strike craft such as fighters and bombers. As a dedicated carrier, it tends to operate towards the rear of an engagement, utilising the superior effective range of its charges to stay out of harm’s way while inflicting appalling damage on the enemy. It also carries a reasonable ship-ship armament in the form of a pair of disruptors, allowing it to defend itself directly if called upon to do so. While Shaltari bombers are undoubtedly dangerous, it’s often the fighters than fulfil the most useful role within a tribal fleet. Since Shaltari point defence is inoperable when a ship’s shields are up, they are often the only counter to enemy close action attack and enemy bombers, especially if they are able to close with the Shaltari and survive the approach. As such, the Basalt is crucial pillar around which many of the bloodiest engagements are planned – a powerful factor, since Shaltari fighters are some of the fastest and most potent known to mankind.

ship.lore: The Turquoise is a class of cruiser designed and constructed by the Shaltari Tribes. Highly unusual, the Turquoise is built around both orbital bombardment and close action assault, a role that no other non-Shaltari vessel shares. As a result, it gives the Shaltari surprising flexibility when launching orbital assaults, it can not only destroy enemy opposition immediately above a bombardment site, but then turn its weaponry against any ground forces that may have landed. This two-part role means the Shaltari can accomplish with one ship what other factions would require two to do, making the most of their low numbers. The Turquoise manages this thanks to its ion storm generators, potent weapons that can either unleash waves of energy against void targets or summon fearsome ion storms to lash at ground assets. Unlike its larger cousins that also carry these generators (the Jet and the Sapphire), the Turquoise has no other armament, forcing it to rely on them for all of its offensive potential.

It is a highly reliable and predictable dealer of death, much like its heavier cousin the Obsidian class. The Granite offers superior speed and reduced cost, making it more practical for general use, especially against valuable smaller ships where use of an Obsidian would frankly be overkill. The Granite is also a better choice during advanced manoeuvres as when it cannot unleash all its weapons, it is the equal of the bulkier ship in Both of its primary weapon hardpoints are occupied by a pair of particle lances, the same weapons which lend its larger cousin superlatively dependable damage dealing ability. This class is the most common capital ship to mount these weapons and is most often the first contact an unfortunate UCM captain will have with these weapons. That captain must learn quickly that armour is no protection and that evasive action is the only means of avoiding a cold, starlit grave.

Armed with a pair of disintegrator banks, the Amber is one of the most well-armed vessels of its tonnage, especially when it can deploy both banks against the same target. It is one of the oldest designs still in service with the Shaltari, as evidenced by the micro-scarring found on their hulls, and by the fact that the UCM has lost more ships to this class than any other in its history. Like all Shaltari vessels, the Amber is equipped with an all-encompassing energy shield that gives it superlative protection against enemy firepower, in addition to point defence capabilities in excess of any equivalent ship from another race. However, both cannot be operated at the same time, giving the Amber, and indeed all Shaltari ships, an obvious weakness.

ship.lore: The Azurite is the most common type of light cruiser encountered during the Reconquest. Much like those of other races, this vessel is somewhat more susceptible to damage than full cruisers, although it gains an advantage in combat speed due to its lighter hull. The Azurite also has the rare advantage of beyond normal vectoring capabilities, allowing it to turn and fire with dizzying speed above what even most frigates are capable of. The makes it a highly dangerous and unpredictable opponent, especially when behind the lines where its lightning turning ability is at its most deadly. It is armed primarily with a pair of disruptors. While far from harmless, these weapons have a constricted fire arc compared to the more destructive disintegrator weapons that fulfil the role of standard guns among Shaltari ships. However, their narrow arc is compensated for by the Azurite’s superlative turning circle. It seems that these weapons were chosen for their lower power consumption, since the extreme manoeuvres the Azurite performs must surely consume vast amounts of energy.

As a result, this ship is just as blisteringly fast and capable in manoeuvre as its sister class, ensuring that it can weave through the battlefield to seek its target and bite at the soft underbelly of its Unlike the more general purpose Azurite though, the Aquamarine has a very specific mission profile, possibly unique to the Shaltari and granted by its highly unorthodox main armament, the Gravity Coils. This pair of weapons emits a narrow beam of gravitic disturbance, dealing focused damage to the victim and playing havoc with its inertia. In turn, this allows the target to be re-vectored as the Shaltari wish, diverting thousands of tons of sharship as if it had been pushed by the invisible hand of a divine being. The Aquamarine therefore has a unique support role as it can repulse enemy ships from friendly ones or place them in an unfavourable position, ready for the Shaltari onslaught.

ship.lore: The Cobalt class homeship is essentially a smaller version of the more ubiquitous Emerald class mothership. Its only purpose is to physically convey Shaltari ground forces to the battlespace, from which they can be teleported to the surface via the Voidgate network. The Cobalt is a faster, lower cost alternative to the Emerald best suited to smaller scale operations. Typically, they are employed when Starchiefs do not wish to or need to put large numbers of lives at risk on the frontline. With the Shaltari, superior technology and almost clairvoyant analysis of enemy dispositions and tactics frequently win the day over sheer numbers.

ship.lore: The Mercury class destroyer features an extremely rare weapon type known as the Pulse Ioniser. These weapons establish an energetic link with the target at close ranges, creating an ionised trail through which energy pulses can be passed, creating ever increasing devastation as long as the link is maintained. An unusual quirk of the weapon is that the potential power of the weapon increases in relation to the density of the target’s armour, ensuring that nothing is safe from its onslaught. This ability makes the Mercury class a superlative hunter of the heaviest armoured ships in an opponent’s fleet, vessels often many times its size. As such, the class typically hunts in packs, using careful tactics and downed shields to close to lethal firing range with the foe. Such tactics make it a favourite with the youngest and brashest of Shaltari captains, individuals who have often only lived out a few lifespans and still have much to prove.

ship.lore: The Chromium class destroyer is unusual in that it features a thermal lance cannon, a weapon very similar to the Burnthrough weapons of more primitive races. Compared to some of the more eldritch armaments employed by the Shaltari, the simple expedient of focusing a sustained high energy laser at a target seems primitive. However, no UCMF admiral would deny the effectiveness of such weapons, often from personal experience! Shaltari equivalents are of course more advanced, featuring shorter burn times and higher armour penetration potential. The fact that such a weapon can be mounted on a destroyer type hull in addition to other weapons is a testament to their advanced technology. However, the fact that these ships see more service with the smaller and less well equipped tribes suggests that such technology is simple for the Shaltari to construct ahead of more outlandish weaponry.

ship.lore: The Gallium is a class of cutter constructed by the Shaltari Tribes, and has garnered a reputation as one of the most insidious vessels ever constructed by the race. Though slower than its Caesium counterparts, the Gallium is feared due to its unique bio-atomiser array weapon. The smaller counterparts of the weapon employed by Shaltari ground troops can vaporise living tissue through stone walls; when employed against a starship's hull, the effect is more creeping, a hit will cause living cells to rupture and build up static charges in electronic systems. Over time, more hits compound these small effects, leading to heart attacks and brain haemorrhaging in crew members, or catastrophic computer malfunctions. Due to the slow buildup required, Galliums close aggressively early in an engagement, the better to begin the process. This has made the Gallium home to more Firstborn crew members than any other Shaltari vessel on record, as they have yet to learn to fear death more than they fear a lack of glory.

Hilariously fast by human standards, even the Scourge cannot outrun them. Though physically fragile even by Shaltari standards, its energy shields may hope to repel any hapless return fire that manages to connect. The Caesium’s capabilities also make it an infamous privateer; lone and rogue Shaltari captains have been known to command packs of these lethal hunters to harass and exploit vulnerable targets for their mysterious ends, or just for the sport of it.

ship.lore: Most Shaltari ground forces reach the surface via Voidgates - ubiquitous, unglamorous ships. Voidgates tend to be lightly armoured and unarmed, making them easy targets. However, as common as these vessels are, sometimes the Shaltari need to guarantee landings planetside, so rely on heavier ships. The Selenium class is one such vessel. It has the transference capacity of a Voidgate, and guns designed to fire out of atmosphere at starships. This allows the Selenium to defend the ground troops deployed through it. These enhanced capabilities and much improved survivability over Voidgates makes the class particularly useful in the thick of heavy fighting, especially given the importance Shaltari place on their own lives. As a result, more of this class have been seen during the Battle for Earth than anywhere else.

In addition, the Shaltari rarely fight defensive actions, making an ordinary monitor-type configuration superfluous. Instead, Shaltari types fulfil a rearguard role. The most frequently seen is the Silicon class, armed with a quad-bank of tilt-able ion cannons, giant versions of those commonly found on Kukri grav-tanks. While these effectively damage ships in higher orbital layers, their true value is in disrupting the power systems of larger ships. This makes the Silicon especially favoured by the type to Starchief who likes taking prizes, or enjoys boarding actions against helpless foes, drifting helplessly in the void.

ship.lore: The Amethyst class frigate is perhaps the most the most aggressive ship in the entire Shaltari arsenal and calls for only the most reckless captains with the greatest bloodlust to command. While most Shaltari vessels shy away from close action engagements (and thus they are not regarded for their close in killing power), the Amethyst embraces them. This puts the class at odds with most of the fleet, leading it to conduct very specific missions and highlighting its potency. Indeed, this rightly feared ship is probably the most dangerous close-action oriented frigate sized vessel yet encountered by the UCM, beyond even those of the Scourge. It is armed with a terrifying microwave array, a cluster of weapons designed to do appalling damage to hull and flesh at close range. Its superheating beams are capable of melting through armour, frying internal components and causing reactors to rupture. There are even stories of a ship’s crew being literally cooked to death through the apparent safety of bulkheads, their blood boiling from every orifice in agonising screams. Furthermore, being entirely energy based, these weapons ignore all point defences that would be raised against them.

Most of its internal structures are interlaced with a complex eldritch projection system designed to boost the effectiveness of the shields of a nearby vessel, as long as those shields are raised. This makes the Opal a highly effective escort ship for larger vessels. As almost all Shaltari elders are obsessed with and focused on the continuation of their ancient lives and as such these ships are highly valued as escorts for flagships. It seems however that despite the Shaltari’s obvious mastery of technology, this vessel is very difficult to produce, making it a particularly appealing prize whenever the tribal fleets fight each other, as it has few weapons of its own to defend itself with.

ship.lore: The Jade class frigate is a more focused design than its cousin, the Topaz. While using the same basic hull, this vessel mounts a single highly dangerous, if restrictive, particle lance. This weapon’s effective fire arc is very narrow, forcing the Jade’s captain to be very deliberate about engaging the enemy. Typically, these fast vessels are assigned to flanking operations against rearguard targets or to attack specific, high value assets in the early stages of a battle. The Jade class is also a favoured choice for small Shaltari raiding parties since isolated targets are picked off with speed and precision before any response can be brought to bear. Its particle lance has a lower destructive power than the weapons of most other Shaltari frigates, but what it lacks in damage potential, it makes up for in armour penetrating ability. Its highly focused and devastating beam can slice through any known armour with contemptuous ease, almost always causing meaningful damage with a successful hit. As a result, it is often used against a heavily armoured opponent, whose protections are meaningless against the Jade’s attentions.

ship.lore: The Topaz is the most common Shaltari frigate design encountered by the UCM and has been seen in use with every known Shaltari tribal fleet. It fulfils a role and mode of attack similar to the standard ‘gun’ armed frigates in other races, such as the Toulon, Harpy and Europa. Like most Shaltari ships, the Topaz features an advanced shield system which can be raised for protection or lowered to take advantage of its very small signature. These shields are crucial if the enemy is able to get close enough to engage, as Shaltari frigates are poorly armoured without them. The Topaz is also the bane of supply convoys, where it wreaks havoc on lightly defended adversaries before melting away on silent running. Its primary armament is a prow mounted Disintegrator bank – a powerful weapon for a ship of its size although restricted to the front quarter in engagement zone. As such, effective positioning is crucial to get the best out of these nimble ships. Their energy weapons do however allow for some variance in facing, making the Topaz more flexible and general purpose than its cousin, the Jade.

ship.lore: The Helium Voidflyer is a slippery adversary and a worrying technological twist in Shaltari naval combat. Troops on the ground are sadly familiar with the aliens’ capricious ability to teleport battlefield-level vehicles in and out of hot zones via their gate network. On a strategic level, naval planers have considered this tech limited to deployment of smaller constructs - not so, it seems. The Helium can leverage the existing voidgate network to teleport across the battlespace instantaneously. That the Helium is orders of magnitude larger than anything previously known to possess this ability has raised concerns at the highest level as to what it means for the future - is this new tech, or have the aliens simply deigned to switch tactics? Either way, the prospect of whole starships vanishing and appearing at will likely chill the blood of any captain, despite the small size and short ranged weapons of this new threat.

ship.lore: These tiny vessels fulfil the role of the corvettes of other races, although they are smaller even than those diminutive ships. They are designed solely to hunt enemy atmospheric assets and are extremely fast. These ships are favoured by the most aggressive Shaltari with the least fear of death and as such are generally crewed by Firstborn Shaltari new to the arts of naval warfare. They have a small crew of just twelve individuals and feature no shields due to their size, their pace and atmospheric capability their best protection against the enemy. Typically, they hunt in packs, utilising their compact but lethal ion cannons to rake the hulls of the larger strike carriers which are their preferred prey. Although not as dangerous as a Corvette alone, their cooperation can quickly reduce the target to so much falling debris in a matter of seconds.

ship.lore: The bizzare nature of these ‘ships’ has resulted in the unique classification of ‘voidgate’, devoid as they are of unique character. Indeed, the Shaltari seem to share this opinion, rarely naming them and or giving them more than a skeleton crew. These vessels loosely fulfil the same tactical role as strike carriers for other races, although they do not actually carry troops. Instead, they merely act as a conduit for Shaltari teleportation, transferring Gates (such as the Eden and the Gaia - Shaltari analogues to dropships) from an orbiting mothership to the atmosphere. Since a voidgate must be present in the immediate vicinity of the dropsite, it must physically move to where the teleported construct(s) are to re-materialise. This removes the risk to the forces before deployment as they are never physically present aboard the voidgate, but are instead aboard a much larger and tougher mothership. Voidgates can also re-route forces between each other once on the ground, affording the Shaltari immense tactical flexibility to counterbalance their low Voidgates also create a substantial field of energetic disturbance in the air. This energy can be unleashed against nearby enemy atmospheric assets, such as strike carriers, dropships or bulk landers and can also take the place of defence batteries in a tactical sense, since the Shaltari have no bulk landers of their own.

ship.lore:
The UCM first encountered the Pungari as part of a Shaltari force during Phase 2 of the Reconquest. Unlike their masters, they were prolific in numbers. In them, the Shaltari found a subservient race to exploit in much the same way they had planned for humanity.

Sightings of Pungari ships were reported shortly afterwards, not all had fallen in with the Shaltari. Apparently, the Pungari are new to starfaring; their blocky ships are primitive yet robust. Instead of the low-crew, high-firepower approach advanced generators afford to other races, the Pungari leverage sheer numbers. Routinely, they hurl thousands into suicidal boarding actions; something Pungari do willingly and, as far as UCM soldiers can tell, with much glee. Their stocky frames may cope with the extreme g-forces involved, unencumbered by too much brain to damage.

When encountering Pungari it is always a coin toss on whether they attack or not. They may try to broker simple alliances, happy to plunge into the wars of other races without expecting much in return, beyond a master to serve in awe.

Hyperyacht Aurorum, launched 2493, was commissioned by Caesar Dun, boss of the East Eden Syndicate. She was uniquely built to impeccable standards, riddled with unregistered spaces, and armed far beyond EAA-sanctioned levels. While using her peerless stealth capabilities to evade justice, he unwittingly dodged the Scourge invasion. After months of shadowing a survivor flotilla, Caesar was garrotted by his lieutenant, who took Aurorum to join the refugees.

Today, Aurorum serves as the flagship of Karl Stieglitz, head of the galaxy's most infamous mercenaries: The Decapitators. This privateer flotilla earned dark renown during the Battle of Earth in the vanguard of the Vega Scrapfleet but is now a gun for hire. Stieglitz has already been approached by Kalium and, it is rumoured, the PHR. The UCM has yet to decide how to respond.

ship.lore:
The Hyperyacht Somniferum is not a sight civilized governments want to see on situation reports. Colloquially known as "the party bus", a spike in crime and illegal substances usually follows in its wake. Somniferum's current owner is the "Master of Ceremonies" Maeby Hy. The Somniferum is almost unrecognisable from its initial configuration as an Eden Aerospace Systems Luxury Liner. Lab explosions, combat damage, and ad-hoc refits have all added to it's hodge-podge appearance.

One of these many changes to the ship is the addition of a peculiar weapon system. While it has no official name, the crew and any who face it have dubbed it "Party Poppers". This weapon system fires armour piercing fragmenting flechettes that disperse airborne narcotics and electromagnetic interference into its target. Far too small and numerous to effectively track, this weapon is able to bypass the majority of a ship's point defences and deliver strikes straight to the hull.

The Somniferum is rarely seen over combat zones, preferring to stick to those planets that are safe enough for civilian travel. While able to defend itself against small time competitors, the ship isn't built for combat. More often than not, the Somniferum will make a hasty exit from a planet as soon as it detects any law enforcement on an intercept course.

ship.lore:
A relentless machine of industry, built to mulch, sift, and extract until its timer runs dry. It drills deep, rips apart rock, and spits out raw profit, indifferent to the hands that keep it running. No legacy, no ownership, just a contract ticking toward expiration. When time is up, it moves on, leaving its crew behind, waiting for the next company to stake its claim on the battered frame. Inside, the workers endure the constant grind, wedged between failing systems and the unyielding demand for productivity. Comfort is non-existent, maintenance is endless.

Equipped with a heavy duty drill and front mounted mining array, this vessel doesn't just extract minerals, it carves deep trenches into asteroid surfaces and space debris, kicking up clouds of pulverized rock and metallic sediment. A network of sediment filters and gravity sifting tanks separates valuable ore from dust before storing the processed materials in its cargo bays.

Prominently displayed on the ship's exterior, the countdown display isn't a warning, it's a fact. The contract will expire, and if it doesn't get topped up, the vessel moves on to whatever comes next. Passed from one mining company to the next, these hand me down workhorses run until their rental contracts dry up. Refurbished just enough to stay functional, they degrade with every transfer, patched, battered, barely space worthy, considered scrap with engines.

Upper management doesn't care about the ship, only the ore it pulls in before time runs out. The crew works under relentless pressure, knowing there's no guarantee of renewal.

When the timer hits zero, it's out of their hands. Either the contract gets extended, or the ship moves on.

Despite its size, the colossal vessel remains a world of tight corridors for its 190 crew members. Dust and grime clings to every surface, settling in forgotten corners and coating equipment in a fine greasy layer. Minimal comforts, constant maintenance, and the daily expectation that something will break.

ship.lore:
A relic from the now liquidated Eden Void Logistics inc, the SLM-9 is a battle tested bulk logistics vessel, trusted for fleet replenishment in high risk environments. Though the company behind its design has since shuttered, the SLM-9 endures as a testament to their engineering prowess and affordability. Its metal cargo frame, hydraulic deployment arms and universal clamps ensure rapid, adaptable resupply of ordnance, fuel, and supplies anywhere. Rugged and inexpensive, the SLM-9 remains a reasonable choice for fleets needing a dependable workhorse at a fraction of the cost of newer models.

Unlike conventional Logistics Vessels that unload cargo gradually, the SLM-9 releases its entire payload in a single, controlled operation. Hydraulic deployment arms manoeuvre the entire cargo bed outward, allowing for structured and efficient transfer without manual unloading.

Built for adaptability, the SLM-9's pincer like grappling arms latch onto ships regardless of docking compatibility. Variable force actuators fine tune pressure, securing a stable hold without compromising hull integrity. Whether resupplying warships or assisting stranded vessels, its clamps ensure critical cargo transfer under any conditions.

The SLM-9's hydraulic deployment arms are its defining feature, but also its greatest liability. If compromised by enemy fire or mechanical failure, the vessel loses its ability to unload cargo entirely, rendering it useless. A damaged deployment system means supplies remain trapped onboard, preventing fleet resupply and turning the ship into dead weight. While reinforced plating offers some protection, direct hits can buckle the arms, leading to catastrophic failure.

Due to its critical vulnerability, the SLM-9 has begun to be phased out in favour of newer resupply haulers with reinforced unloading mechanisms and modular backup systems. The remaining SLM-9 units are considered outdated relics, still operational but increasingly rare.

ship.lore:
The T-Type was once a common sight across many shipyards. Due to the size of many pre-war ships, a way of moving these gargantuan vessels out of drydock was needed. T-Types were devised to be the answer to this sizeable problem. The first batch of these floated out of the assembly lines prior to the first Pathfinder, ready and waiting to guide it to a safe launching point. Since then, countless multitudes of these ships have been constructed. Most serve their entire service life in the void, however some are refitted as lunar landers once their superstructure becomes unusable for its intended purpose.

Only a small amount of these were refit with foldspace drives, the majority were only designed to work around a single planet and its satellites. Those that were refit tend to be found in independent fleets, where they assist in swapping components on their larger vessels. T-Types are not built for any form of combat, though their internal bracing gives them a certain resilience, they are unable to weather any attack from dedicated combat ships.

Some T-Types have been converted to function similarly to mines, albeit with a much more personal weapon system. These have weaponised their towing ability, captains with a death wish will attach their tug to an enemy vessel and set their engines to full. When performed right, this can violently tear vessels in half, though at the cost of the tugboat and its crew.

ship.lore:
The DH-Type represents one of the Colonial Fleet's largest run of dedicated long-range prison ships, built around a standardized architecture of reinforced armour, multi-tier detention decks and automated security. Originally intended strictly for high-risk inmate transport and remote incarceration, wartime pressures pushed the class into broader operational roles.

Though designed with consistent core systems, such as compartmentalized containment blocks, automated defensive suites, ECM shielding, and a C.A.G.E emitter field. The ships grew increasingly variable due to differing missions, retrofits, and partial deactivations. Although uncommon, Individual DH-Type vessels gained their own notoriety, such as Iron Veil, Remnant Forge, Dreadhold and Bright Spire. The DH-Type ships illustrated the evolution through conversions into troop transports, logistics carriers, medical ships, and frontier support platforms, often retaining traces of their original penal infrastructure.

In modern service, L1-class hulls endure as adaptable, if austere, multi-role assets. Their durable construction, intimidating infrastructure, and legacy security systems continue to define their operational character, reflecting both the robustness of the original design and the fleet's ongoing need to repurpose coercive architecture for broader demands.

ship.lore:
The Jah'tar are an independent, if diminished, starfaring race that sails from the planet Jaheria. Over two century's peaceable trade with the UCM's colony of Platina, they have shared some of their history.

Their Time of Many Worlds ended roughly three millennia ago when the Great Adversary came. The Jah'tar do not know if any of their other planets survived. Their lifespans of roughly 35 years make this race-memory dimmer than one might expect, but parallels to mankind's own experience was clear, the Scourge were the likely culprits. Surviving artworks show cruder invading ships, but some Jah'tar technology bears limited similarity to Scourge, and most scientists believe it was absorbed and evolved by the enemy. Jah'tar ships also appear grown rather than made, although theirs are largely pseudo-organic chitin over a fine titanium weave.

The Jah'tar no longer fully understand their own technology. Possibly such knowledge was confined to their lost central worlds, but as in antiquity, all Jah'tar works radiate a passion for style and beauty. They covet precious materials and gems, driving their trade with Platina. In return, the UCM gains access to the Jaherian System's ores and wealth of rare elements essential for FTL drive core construction.

The Jah'tar are rangier than humans with stronger limbs and thick, leathery skin. Naturally placid and artistic, they move in an unhurried way but are fast when pressed. With long, prehensile tails they are agile climbers, leading to some exotic spaces aboard their ships. Their four, quad-jointed digits are equally dextrous on hands or feet, and are in constant motion, possibly as a base layer of communication. Their language is a series of rapid clicks and screeches, so they use human speech in negotiations out of respect for our limited vocal range.

Most of humanity's contact with the Jah'tar is via their famous Startraders, graceful, cruiser-sized ships with lavishly decorated meeting spaces, living areas, and cavernous holds. These vessels are permitted free passage within the Platina System but are closely monitored whenever they appear elsewhere in UCM space, despite being unarmed. Hawkish colonial admirals insist that all that internal space could be put to more nefarious uses. Some Startraders serve as mercenaries with other races in exchange for favourable trades, although the UCM occasionally utilises their services so too. Their value lies with their unique support technologies since the Jah'tar refuse to license any true warships to other's violence.

Relations with the alien Jah'tar is an aberration for the UCM, but these arrangements go back before the Scourge invasion and are frankly easier than conquest. Although Jaheria would inevitably be crushed, Jah'tar weaponry is formidable when they are forced to use it, and high casualties that humanity can ill-afford would result.

ship.lore:
M-Type Barges are the larger cousin of the L-Type. Produced at the same Tharsis Manufacturing shipyards over Mars, the M-Type was designed for corporate bulk shipping. Many and more of these were owned and operated by the enduring shipping companies of old Earth, each of them emblazoned with corporate livery. Designed and built after the L-Type, these ships feature much improved Foldspace drives as well as the latest innovations in structural bracing. Optimisations in production brought the build time on these freight behemoths down to only twice that of the L-Type.

Many of these were spared the events of the Scourge invasion, most would have been slowly moving between the colonies and the cradle worlds, far enough away to make emergency jumps to safety. The initial trade and logistics network of the UCM was built upon the backs of the M-Type, their reliability and availability gave the colonies enough trade stability to recover from the loss of the cradle worlds. M-Types are surprisingly rare in Resistance fleets, most of the captains of these ships were more interested in meeting deadlines and quotas than in doomsday predictions prior to the battle of Vega. Kalium is yet to be seen operating these ships, preferring the L-Type for combat resupply, though may potentially be using M-Types in more secure Kalium controlled systems.

Recent developments in prefabricated defensive structures have allowed a small number of these ships to carry deployable missile defence outposts in place of their normal cargo compliment. These outposts are designed to grant a foothold on a planet and supplement its missile halo while more permanent structures are built, re-purposed, or captured.

These ships travel discreetly between remote depots, derelict battlefields, and disposal zones. Crewed by an extensive team of highly trained specialists under strict quarantine and secrecy protocols, The Oblivion barge handles cargo that is often poorly understood or classified. ship.lore:
The Type-87 Terminus Harvester is a colossal reclamation vessel built to consume the unrepairable wreckage of war. Its monolithic maw engulfs chunks up to frigate tonnage, feeding them into vast crushing chambers where superheated hydraulic presses obliterate hull plating to slag. Two VX-22 Flensers detach from its hull, peeling derelicts apart and hauling scraps to their final destruction. Ancient, slow-moving, and relentless, it labours, stripping vessels down to raw material. Within its corroded halls, life is harsh. Dim corridors reek of burning metal as air filters struggle against decades of industrial smog.

The Type-87's wedge-like prow is battered and scarred, worn from decades of grinding through wreckage. Deep gouges and warped plating mark where debris crumpled beneath its relentless push, clearing the way for the behemoth behind.

A monolithic opening capable of engulfing entire frigates, feeding them into a crushing chamber spanning the volume of a megastructure. Inside, reinforced walls lined with titanic hydraulic presses grind vessels down in a superheated maelstrom of pulverized metal, reducing all to molten slag.

Equipped with two VX-22 Flensers, these small salvage vessels dock onto the Harvester's hull when idle but detach to roam wreckage fields. They Brutally peel derelicts apart piecemeal while hauling fragmented components to the crushing maw. Though technically separate, they operate as an extension of the Harvester, ensuring no usable scrap escapes consumption.

ship.lore:
The VX-22 Flensers are compact salvage vessels designed for brutal ship dismantling. Their prow mounted sawblades don't cut cleanly, they tear, shred, and rip through wreckage with unrestrained violence. Designed for aggressive reclamation, they are the smaller, more aggressive sibling to the T-Type Tugboat. Where the Tugboat manoeuvres and stabilizes wreckage for controlled processing, the Flensers gut derelicts with reckless brutality, prioritizing destruction over precision.

Heavy rotating saws brutally cut through hull plating, breaking it into manageable pieces and scattering debris as they progress. Instead of delicate incision, the Flensers' sawblades operate at maximum torque, chewing through reinforced bulkheads with enough force to buckle surrounding structure.

Their cutting mechanisms frequently overheat, causing violent energy surges that make their hulls shudder mid operation.

The Flenser hurls debris into the Type-87 Terminus Harvester's compactor bay, sometimes suffering brutal kickback as the churning machinery spits chunks back out. When it happens, the debris slams into its failing frame, worsening the damage and making every load a gamble.

Positioned below the cockpit, this reinforced plating shields pilots from wreckage kicked up during cutting operations. Sloped for maximum deflection, it redirects debris that could slam into the hull with deadly force, absorbing impacts before they buckle metal or breach compartments.

ship.lore:
A monolithic vessel of unimaginable scale, the Provenance Ark dwarfs most ships. A precursor to the modular construction found on Coloniser class vessels, these ships were a talisman of hope and expansionism. These are the first major terraforming vessels built by mankind, reaching out into an unknown universe. Built to prepare entire worlds for habitation, it carries vast stores of genetic material, atmospheric stabilizers, and autonomous resource systems. The Ark monitors planetary progress through an extensive network of sensors and automated regulators, adjusting atmospheric composition, maintaining microbial balance, and even modulating gravitational and magnetic fields to stabilize emerging terrains.

Entire cities once mere schematics, rise, with power grids, transport arteries, and habitation modules ready long before the first settlers arrive. Inside, Construction drones and biotic cultivators orchestrate the birth of forests, oceans, and breathable atmospheres with the precision of a master artisan.

Many ships of this class feature underslung terraforming torpedo launchers. While near useless in ship to ship combat, these torpedoes are geared towards atmospheric re-entry and contain a plethora of mutagens and nerve agents, some of which would be used on Senator class battlecruisers. Under normal circumstances the use of these would constitute a war crime. Here they are simply used to rid prospective landing areas of their megafauna, causing mass hysteria and aggression in local fauna. Any issues with unruly creatures take care of themselves, and those left over can be cut down by specialised anti-fauna vehicles. Once the LZ is cleared of hostiles, the terraformer can then deploy more traditional terraforming methods.

ship.lore:
The EX-7 Packet-Runner is a common courier craft used throughout the territories of the United Colonies of Mankind. Designed for routine parcel and sensitive package transport, it prioritizes simple construction and dependable operation over appearance or refinement. Most examples in service are visibly beaten up and poorly maintained, their worn hulls reflecting constant use and minimal upkeep.

They are Built around a straightforward modular frame, similar to other workhorse craft like the T-Type utility haulers and the smaller VX-22 Flesners. The EX-7 typically consists of little more than the essentials: cockpit, drive assembly, and standardized cargo racks bolted into a compact hull with the cargo containers mounted underneath.

Though rarely the focus of attention, EX-7 Packet-Runners move a constant flow of everyday freight between stations, depots, and outposts, quietly handling the unglamorous but essential task of keeping day-to-day logistics running. Colonial authorities have repurposed many of these ships for the express purpose of resupplying fighter and bomber support craft. Their cargo containers filled with factory-fresh compliments of fighters and bombers waiting for an appropriate launch platform. Experimental versions of these containers have been developed to effortlessly convert standardised hardpoints on space stations into makeshift hangar bays.

ship.lore:
Though there has been extensive speculation on the viability or even potential existence of any kind of life adapted for the vacuum of space, none have been able to prove any hypothesis one way or another. The complete alien nature of something that could feasibly live without any kind of atmosphere or gravity pushes the limits of human speculation. Though themselves alien, every other race humanity has encountered has had a terrestrial origin. PHR expeditionary fleets have almost by accident stumbled into proof of space-based lifeforms. A solitary, anomalous creature was found in a small orange dwarf system. For an as-yet-unknown reason, this creature was traversing a veritable cosmic backwater with nought but ice and gas giants. Seemingly passive, the creature ignored the survey fleet, at least until it closed in. Initially curious, the creature allowed a single survey vessel close enough to scan, though was likely taking in all it could of the strange mechanical interloper.

It's temperament suddenly changed, however, when a second survey vessel moved to its opposite flank. Without warning, it unleashed a tentacle that damn near tore the closest ship in half. If it wasn't for the quick thinking of the crew the ship could well have been lost to the attack. The flanking ship was hit by an attack with no discernible origin. Crushing forces impacted the ship and though little structural damage was caused, they were pushed into a completely different heading and at a much reduced velocity.

Fortunately both ships had completed detailed scans of the creature, and although these are currently highly classified, news of this incredible discovery, now dubbed "The Argonaut", is reaching the ears of those back in the republic. Unfortunately, both survey ships have been prevented from returning to PHR space and have been instructed to seek the nearest safe-haven to repair and shelter. While the Solar system is hardly safe, it is the largest concentration of PHR assets within a reasonable distance, and is about as safe as anywhere else.
